title: NIST: standard atomic weight of Uranium (U, Z=92) is 238.02891(3)
summary: NIST prints the standard atomic weight field of Uranium (U, Z=92) as 238.02891(3), with the isotope rows in the same file.
body: PubChem's periodic-table row names atomic number 92, symbol U, as Uranium. The NIST compositions file prints the standard atomic weight of Uranium as 238.02891(3). The parenthesis is the uncertainty NIST prints on the last digits of that standard atomic weight. It is an evaluated standard, not one laboratory weighing of one sample. Geological materials are known in which the element has an isotopic composition outside the limits for normal material. The difference between the atomic weight of the element in such materials and that given in the table may exceed the stated uncertainty. Modified isotopic compositions may be found in commercially available material because the material has been subjected to an undisclosed or inadvertent isotopic fractionation. Substantial deviations in atomic weight of the element from that given in the table can occur. Isotope rows in the same file: U-233 relative atomic mass 233.0396355(29), isotopic composition blank; U-234 relative atomic mass 234.0409523(19), isotopic composition 0.000054(5); U-235 relative atomic mass 235.0439301(19), isotopic composition 0.007204(6); U-236 relative atomic mass 236.0455682(19), isotopic composition blank; U-238 relative atomic mass 238.0507884(20), isotopic composition 0.992742(10). A relative atomic mass is scaled to carbon-12. An isotopic composition, when the field is not blank, is a representative mole fraction, not a new assay made for this card. The symbols for an interval, a parenthesis, a bracket, and a # mark are defined on world.chemistry.nist-atomic-weight-notation. This standard atomic weight is not the Chemistry WebBook molecular-weight field, which is a different catalog entry when one exists.
